title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: Real estate is not one business; it is a portfolio of micro-markets, each with its own buyer psychology, approval bottleneck, and margin structure.
epigraph.author: Mumbai Micro-Market Primer

web_blocks.html: Ajmera Realty operates across two core product verticals: Residential Development and Commercial & Boutique Office Spaces [11][14]. Residential spans mid-income, premium, and luxury apartments, while commercial targets progressive strata sales and selective annuity retention [11][14]. Execution relies on four land-sourcing models: owned legacy land, society redevelopment, SRA projects, and JV/JDA partnerships [11]. Geographically, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) drives most current sales and future Gross Development Value (GDV) [14]. A focused two-cluster Bengaluru footprint (Electronic City and Yelahanka) plus selective Pune and Ahmedabad projects round out the portfolio [1][6][14].

web_blocks.takeaway: Owned-land residential in Wadala generates the highest margins, while MMR redevelopment and Bengaluru JVs provide capital-light volume diversification.

web_blocks.html: Segment 1 — Owned Legacy Township Residential (Example: Ajmera Manhattan I & II, Wadala East): Ajmera Manhattan sits inside the 100-acre Ajmera i-Land township next to the 25-acre Bhakti Park garden [4][15]. It targets affluent upgraders, doctors, business owners, and executives working in BKC, Lower Parel, and South Mumbai [4][15]. Phase 1 (MahaRERA P51800032948, 543 units across two 44-storey towers) offers 2, 3, and 4 BHK homes [15][16]. Carpet areas run ~750 to 1,866 sq ft at ₹30,000–37,000 per sq ft, or ₹2.5 crore to ₹6.5+ crore per unit [14][15]. Because Ajmera acquired the land decades ago, it avoids the ₹10,000–15,000 per sq ft FSI cost paid in nearby MMRDA auctions [11]. That legacy basis supports project-level EBITDA margins above 30% [11]. Manhattan I reached 95% sales by Q2 FY27 and nears OC completion in FY27 [14]. Manhattan II (MahaRERA PR1180002500822, 440 units) sold over 40% (~₹700 crore) within 20 days of its September 2025 launch and stood 56% sold by September 2026 [10][14][16]. Nearby, Ajmera Greenfinity Phase 2 (MahaRERA P51800052226, 172 units) reached 94%+ sales [14][16].

Segment 2 — Capital-Light MMR Redevelopment & JV Residential (Example: Ajmera Vihara & Ajmera Solis): To scale beyond Wadala without tying up equity in land, Ajmera bids on central-suburb society and SRA redevelopments [11]. At Ajmera Vihara (Bhandup West), it builds 1 BHK and 2.5 BHK homes priced from ₹71 lakh to ₹2+ crore for salaried buyers along LBS Marg and the Eastern Express Highway [17]. Ajmera must construct free rehab units alongside saleable inventory; the rehab slab reached the 9th floor by Q2 FY26 [11]. Redevelopment projects carry thinner EBITDA margins—temporarily compressing consolidated margins to 26–29%—but require minimal upfront land capex [11]. Ajmera Solis Phase 1 in Vikhroli East achieved 84% absorption within 60 hours of launch and reached 87% sold by Q2 FY27 [14][18]. Ajmera Eden in Ghatkopar received its OC ahead of schedule at 98% sold [14]. In contrast, luxury redevelopment in Versova (Vann / One by Ajmera, MahaRERA PR1180002502178, 125 units of 1,700–2,000+ sq ft) reached just 4% sold, showing micro-market price limits [10][14][16].

Segment 3 — Commercial & Boutique Offices (Example: Ajmera Sikova & Wadala Boutique Office): Ajmera builds commercial towers for strata sale to SMEs, clinics, and regional offices [2][13]. Examples include the 14-storey Ajmera ICRC / Sikova center in Ghatkopar West (85%+ sold) and a 1 lakh+ sq ft wing at Ajmera Nucleus in Bengaluru [2][13]. Its newest commercial bets are Thirty 3.15 (33 West) in Bandra (25% sold by Q2 FY27) and a flagship Boutique Office tower at Wadala [14]. In Q3 FY26, management revised the Wadala Boutique Office plan under Maharashtra's Regulation 33(20)-B PAP FSI scheme [18]. That revision expanded carpet area from 6 lakh sq ft to 16 lakh sq ft and lifted GDV from ₹1,800 crore to ₹5,300–5,500 crore at ~₹4,000–5,000/sq ft incremental FSI cost [18]. Management plans to sell smaller boutique offices progressively to self-fund construction while keeping larger floor plates for recurring rent [18].

Segment 4 — Bengaluru & Regional Clusters (Example: Ajmera Iris, Electronic City Phase 2): In Bengaluru, Ajmera operates through 70%-owned JVs under Ajmera Housing Corporation Bangalore across Electronic City and Yelahanka [6]. At Ajmera Iris (Electronic City Phase 2, Karnataka RERA PRM/KA/RERA/1251/310/PR/281024/007184), it is building 215 mid-market 2 and 3 BHK homes across 4.7 acres (1,58,859 sq ft) [6][19]. Priced at ₹1.0 crore to ₹1.26 crore for IT employees, Iris reached 94% sales and 73%+ completion by mid-FY27 [6][14][19]. Buyers should note its RERA certificate lists December 2026 completion, while investor decks cite December 2028 [6][14]. In Yelahanka, Ajmera Marina (PRM/KA/RERA/1251/309/PR/310125/007461, 2,18,670 sq ft) reached 76% sold by Q2 FY27 [6][14]. Outside Bengaluru, Ajmera holds Casa Vyoma in Vastrapur, Ahmedabad (2–4 BHKs at ₹1.23–2.70 crore) and upcoming redevelopment/SRA projects in Vishrantwadi, Pune [14][20].

web_blocks.title: Margin Mix Effect: Owned Land vs. Redevelopment
paragraphs: Management cautions that consolidated EBITDA margins swing quarter-to-quarter with revenue-recognition mix [11]. When lower-margin Bengaluru JVs and Bhandup redevelopment (Vihara) cross the Ind AS 115 threshold, OPM dips toward 25–26%, as seen in Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY27 [8][11]. When Wadala owned-land projects like Manhattan I dominate recognition, OPM expands back above 30% [8][11].

book_paragraphs: To understand how Ajmera Realty makes money, you have to stop thinking of it as a generic 'real estate company' and instead picture four distinct engines running under one roof. The crown jewel is its owned legacy land in Wadala East, known as Ajmera i-Land. Think of a 100-acre enclave in central Mumbai where the land was bought decades ago at historical prices. When Ajmera launches a 44-storey twin-tower project like Ajmera Manhattan here, selling 2, 3, and 4 BHK apartments (750 to 1,866 sq ft carpet area) to BKC executives and South Mumbai upgraders at ₹30,000 to ₹37,000 per square foot, the land cost on the income statement is practically zero. While nearby competitors bidding on MMRDA plots must absorb ₹10,000 to ₹15,000 per square foot just for FSI rights, Ajmera pockets that spread as gross margin.

The second engine is capital-light redevelopment and Slum Rehabilitation Authority (SRA) work across Mumbai's central and western suburbs. Take Ajmera Vihara in Bhandup West, where salaried families buy 1 BHK and 2.5 BHK homes starting around ₹71 lakh. Here, Ajmera does not buy the land outright; instead, it builds free rehab apartments for existing society members or slum dwellers in exchange for the right to sell the free-sale tower. The return on capital is attractive because very little equity sits idle in land, yet the accounting EBITDA margin is noticeably thinner because the construction cost of the rehab building is baked into the project economics.

The third engine is commercial and boutique office development, anchored by completed projects like Sikova in Ghatkopar West and upcoming launches like Thirty 3.15 in Bandra and the massive Wadala Boutique Office. Notice the clever financing twist management revealed in FY26: by utilizing Maharashtra's PAP FSI scheme, Ajmera expanded the Wadala Boutique Office from 6 lakh to 16 lakh square feet, lifting its gross development value to roughly ₹5,300–5,500 crore. Rather than locking up ₹1,000 crore of debt to build a pure lease-only office tower, Ajmera plans to sell smaller boutique office units progressively on a milestone-linked payment schedule—just like residential flats—to fund construction, while retaining larger floor plates for long-term annuity rent.

Finally, there is the Bengaluru and regional mid-market engine, operating through 70%-owned joint ventures in two specific Bengaluru pockets: Electronic City and Yelahanka, alongside selective projects in Ahmedabad (Casa Vyoma) and Pune (Vishrantwadi). At Ajmera Iris in Electronic City Phase 2, 215 apartments priced between ₹1 crore and ₹1.26 crore cater directly to IT professionals who want branded construction without luxury pricing. It is a steady, high-turnover business—94% sold within two years of launch—that diversifies Ajmera away from Mumbai's cyclicality, even though it carries lower margins than Wadala.

book_callouts.title: Why Location Determines Margin More Than Construction
book_callouts.text: A square foot of concrete and steel costs roughly the same to pour in Bhandup as it does in Wadala, yet Wadala commands double the selling price on near-zero historical land cost. Watching the revenue mix between Wadala and suburban redevelopment tells you where quarterly margins are headed.

book_callouts.title: Check the Contracting Entity in Bengaluru
book_callouts.text: In Bengaluru, Ajmera builds through 70% joint ventures under Ajmera Housing Corporation Bangalore. While the brand is the same, the economic share and RERA counterparty sit at the JV level.

book_subsections.title: Where Velocity Splits: Mid-Income vs. Luxury
paragraphs: A crucial lesson from Ajmera's FY26–FY27 execution is that the brand's sweet spot sits squarely in mid-income and upper-mid-income housing (₹1 crore to ₹5 crore). When Ajmera launched Solis in Vikhroli East, buyers snapped up 84% of Phase 1 within 60 hours. When it launched Manhattan II in Wadala, over 40% sold in 20 days. Both projects offered clear connectivity, recognizable township or suburban infrastructure, and ticket sizes that fit dual-income Mumbai households.

By contrast, when the company stepped into pure luxury redevelopment at Vann (One by Ajmera) in Versova with 1,700-to-2,000-plus square foot apartments, initial sales crawled to just 4% by September 2026. Similarly, its Vasai project stalled against intense local competition where buyers preferred under-construction discounts. That divergence is healthy to observe: it shows where Ajmera's brand commands pricing power and where it remains a price-taker.
